recipes.name: Chicken fajitas

ingredients.note: toasted in a dry pan until they pop

daughter.note: corpus describes her plate but gives no figures

leftover.note: Eat cold, in a wrap or over salad. Reheating toughens the chicken.

method: Get the pan properly hot before anything goes in, then the chicken in a single layer — don't crowd it or it steams instead of colouring. At this quantity that is two batches, 6 minutes each.
Peppers and onion in for 4–5 minutes, keeping some bite.
Spices in for the last minute with a splash of water so they toast rather than burn.
Lime squeezed over at the table, off the heat — cooked into the pan you can't taste it.
Toasted pumpkin seeds over at the table.

tips.text: Everyone else builds a wholemeal wrap with chicken, cheese and salsa. Jon's plate is the chicken as a bowl with half a tin of black beans stirred in, salsa, and one wrap or none.
Eat the leftovers cold, in a wrap or over salad. Reheating toughens the chicken and turns the peppers limp.

recipes.name: Bolognese with hidden red lentils

ingredients.note: weighed into the pan at the end
pangrattato: fried in a little oil until hard and deep brown

daughter.note: 0.87 of Jon's portion, about 40g of dry pasta in it

leftover.note: Reheats better than the day it was made.

method: Onion and grated carrot into the oil for 6 minutes, then the garlic for one minute more.
Mince in and browned properly — 6 or 7 minutes without constant stirring. Colour is flavour.
Purée in and cooked out for a minute, then the tomatoes, the rinsed dry lentils, the herbs, the Worcestershire sauce and the water.
Simmer 25–30 minutes, stirring now and then — the lentils catch if left alone. Weigh {{3}}g of salt into the whole pan at the end rather than seasoning by eye.
Pangrattato over each bowl — breadcrumbs fried hard in a little oil.

tips.text: Red lentils and grated carrot dissolve into the sauce and carry most of its fibre. Your daughter has spotted dissolved lentils before, so cook them down well.
It reheats better than the day it was made.

jon.note: raw sum 662g on the plate; a baked potato loses ~25% of its water

leftover.note: a reheated jacket goes leathery - cook the number you will eat

method: Oven to 200°C. Prick the potatoes and rub them with the oil and the {{2}}g of coarse salt.
Straight onto the oven shelf for 60–75 minutes, until the skins are crisp. No foil — it steams the skin.
While they bake, soak the diced red onion in a squeeze of lemon for 5 minutes, and toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan until they start to pop.
Tuna mayo: mix the Skyr, mayonnaise and Dijon, then stir in the tuna, cornichons and onion.
Warm the beans.
Split the potatoes and add a scrape of butter. Everyone builds their own: tuna mayo, beans, sweetcorn and cheddar, then the mackerel flaked over and the seeds on top. Salad on the side.

tips.text: Short on time? Microwave the potatoes for 6 minutes first, then 30 minutes in the hot oven. The skins still crisp.
Cook only the number you'll eat. A reheated jacket goes leathery.

Toasted flaked almonds scattered over.

Greens through the hot lentils, lemon over everything.

recipes.name: Chicken, pepper and potato traybake

ingredients.note: onto the tray with everything else for the last 10 minutes, not plated separately
pangrattato: fried in a little oil until hard and deep brown

jon.note: raw sum 871g; roasting takes ~18% off

leftover.note: Good cold, sliced over salad.

method: Oven to 200°C. Potatoes in first, on their own, tossed in half the oil and half of the {{2}}g of weighed salt. 20 minutes.

Meanwhile rub the chicken with the remaining oil, the spices and the rest of the salt. Butterfly the breasts or bash them to an even thickness — an untouched breast is thick at one end and thin at the other, and the thin end is dry before the thick end is cooked.
After 20 minutes add the peppers and onion, sit the chicken on top, and back in for 20–22 minutes.
Lemon over everything. Rest the chicken 5 minutes before slicing.
Pangrattato over the tray at the end, with the lemon zest through it.

tips.text: Give the potatoes 20 minutes on their own first — that's what stops the chicken drying out.
Keep Jon's potatoes to about 200g. More makes the plate too filling.

ingredients.note: boiled 4 minutes and stirred through at the end

jon.note: 252g raw thigh, 212g raw potato, 117g asparagus, 71g edamame

daughter.note: 181g chicken, 152g wedges, asparagus if she'll have it. Salt derived from her glaze share

leftover.note: The wedges go soft overnight — eat it cold with the chicken sliced over rather than reheating.

method: {{35}}ml of reduced-salt soy, the tomato purée, the honey and the crushed garlic in a bag or bowl with the chicken, 15 minutes minimum — the honey needs that long to do anything.
Oven to 200°C. Wedges tossed in the teaspoon of oil and {{1}}g of salt weighed across the whole potato tray, on their own tray, 25 minutes.
Chicken into an ovenproof dish with its marinade for 35 minutes, started at the same time as the wedges.
Asparagus onto the wedge tray for the last 5–8 minutes. Edamame from frozen into boiling water for 4.
Toasted sesame over the chicken.

tips.text: Thighs, not breast — but breast works. Thigh survives 35 minutes in the oven better and holds a glaze; breast at that length wants butterflying or it dries.
The edamame is doing the fibre: 4g for 96 calories, the best trade available here.
Good cold the next day, sliced, with the wedges left behind. Reheated wedges go soft.

toasted in a dry pan until they colour

leftover.note: cold, flaked through the vegetables

Courgette, red onion and garlic in with the remaining oil. 10 more minutes.

Toasted flaked almonds over.

recipes.name: Baked meatballs with ciabatta

ingredients.note: bought; pick the lowest-salt pack you can find
rinsed; into the stock 10 minutes before the tomatoes

pangrattato: fried in a little oil until hard and deep brown
browned with the meatballs and left in the sauce

leftover.note: one portion without the bread

method: Brown the ready-made meatballs — about {{450}}g — in the oil in an ovenproof pan until coloured on most sides, then set aside. Brown the {{250}}g of 5% mince in the same pan, breaking it up, and leave it in. Add no salt anywhere — the meatballs bring it.
Onion, garlic and thyme into the same pan until soft, scraping up what the meatballs left behind.
Lentils and the stock in first — simmer 10 minutes before the tomatoes go in. Tomato stops red lentils breaking down, and lentils that stay whole are the ones your daughter spots.
Tomatoes and basil in, simmered uncovered 15–20 minutes until reduced by a quarter.
Oven to 200°C. Meatballs into the sauce for 10 minutes, cheese over, back in until it melts. Basil, then to the table with the wholemeal ciabatta.
Pangrattato over the top before serving.

tips.text: The meatballs are the salt in this dish. Buy the lowest-salt pack you can find and add none.
Lentils in the stock before the tomatoes, so they break down and thicken the sauce.
A 31g piece of wholemeal ciabatta is enough to wipe the plate.

recipes.name: One-pot sticky coconut chicken rice
recipes.wholegrainException: Method, not preference. Brown rice needs 35-45 minutes at ~2.5:1 liquid; this dish cooks jasmine at a deliberately reduced 1.5:1 for 20-25 minutes and the crust is the point. The chicken sits on the rice the whole cook and thighs are shredded at 40 minutes. The gain would be 1.1g of fibre on a 55g dry portion.

ingredients.note: brands vary a lot in salt — pick a lower one

ingredients.item: Choy sum, pak choi or tenderstem

jon.note: 272g raw thigh, 41g dry rice, 337g greens, 15g peanuts. No longer the saltiest plate in the corpus - the bean and spinach pot took that at 3.19g

daughter.note: 234g chicken, 35g dry rice, greens - no chilli, coriander or peanuts. Salt derived from her sauce share

leftover.note: Rice: cool it fast, fridge within the hour, reheat once until piping hot — never in a flask.

method: Heavy pot over medium-high, sprayed. Chicken 2 minutes a side until lightly golden, then out and kept warm.
{{40}}g of red curry paste and the coriander stalks into the same pot for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Rice in, stirred to coat. Then {{14}}ml of fish sauce, the {{253}}ml of coconut milk and the {{153}}ml of boiling water.
Chicken back on top in a single layer. Bring to the boil, then the lowest simmer, lid on, 20–25 minutes until a crust forms on the bottom. Don't lift the lid.
Fork the rice through gently, greens over the top, lid back on, 5 minutes off the heat to steam.
Slice the chicken. Coriander leaves, the weighed peanuts, lime, chilli oil if you want it.

tips.text: Don't change the balance of coconut milk, water and rice — it's what forms the crust.
Jasmine rice, not brown — brown won't cook or crust in this time.
Weigh the peanuts. 15g is 87 calories; a casual handful is 40g and 230.
Any spare: cool it fast, refrigerate within the hour, reheat once and piping hot.

Toasted almonds over.

recipes.name: Roast broccoli soup with halloumi croutons

ingredients.note: roughly chopped, stalks included - the stalks are a third of the head
not stock — the parmesan rind and porcini give the flavour
150g a bowl, DOLLOPED ON TOP - never stirred through

leftover.note: Six portions of about 450g. Freezes well — add the Skyr at the bowl, not before.

method: Oven to 200°C. Broccoli on trays in a single layer, sprayed, 15 minutes — two trays at this quantity. Roasting is the whole recipe: boiled broccoli soup is a different, worse thing.
Potatoes into a big pan with the water, the parmesan rind and the porcini with its soaking liquor. Simmer 15 minutes until tender, then fish out the rind.
Roasted broccoli in for 5 more minutes, then blend smooth. {{5}}g of salt weighed into the whole batch and plenty of pepper.
Cool fast and portion it here: six tubs, roughly 450g each. Three days in the fridge, three months in the freezer.

At the bowl: reheat a portion, then 150g of Skyr dolloped on top, not stirred through. Halloumi in a dry non-stick pan 3–4 minutes with the honey over for the last 30 seconds. Croutons and lemon zest on.

tips.text: The soup freezes because there's no dairy in it — that's why the Skyr goes on at the bowl.
Use the stalks, peeled and diced. They cook down to nothing and they're a third of the head.

prep.note: Six tubs from one 45-minute cook. Three days in the fridge, three months in the freezer.
prep.pan: The halloumi croutons are four minutes in a dry pan at the bowl. On a busy day, have the soup plain.

recipes.name: Smoky chicken and chickpea braise - the flask lunch

ingredients.note: bloomed in dry fat, not stirred into liquid
0.6g a portion; the only salt in the dish
goes in AT THE FLASK, not in the pan
toasted in a dry pan until they pop

leftover.note: Four portions from one cook.

method: Oil into a wide pan over high heat, chicken in one layer — two batches at this quantity, 4 minutes a side without moving it. This browning is most of the flavour and it is the step people skip. Out onto a plate.
Onion into the same pan for 5 minutes, scraping the brown off the base. Garlic and all three spices for 60 seconds — dry heat before any liquid or the paprika stays raw and chalky.
Peppers, passata, stock, chickpeas, the {{2.4}}g of weighed salt and the chicken back in with anything it has leaked. Simmer uncovered 20 minutes until it thickens and a spoon leaves a trail.
Cool fast and portion into four tubs. The lemon and parsley go in at the flask in the morning, not now — a squeeze of acid that has sat in the fridge for three days tastes of nothing.
Toasted pumpkin seeds in a twist of foil, added at the flask. They cannot travel in the braise or they soften.

tips.text: Scald the flask with boiling water and fill it above 75°C. It will still be above 60°C at 1pm, which is what makes this safe on a London day.
A thick braise holds heat in a flask far better than soup does.
Don't skip the browning or the lemon — they're what make it taste seasoned.

Beans and stock in. Mash about a quarter of the beans against the side of the pan — that is the step that makes it a braise rather than fish sitting in soup, and it takes ten seconds.

recipes.name: Piri-piri butterflied chicken, crushed potato and pea, charred hispi

less in the daughter's share of the marinade

Hispi quarters cut side down in a dry hot pan or on a hot tray with the remaining oil, 6 minutes without moving them. You want black edges: char on brassica is not a mistake, it is the flavour.

ingredients.note: dry weight; toast it dry for 2 minutes first

doing the salt, which is why the dish needs none added
zest and juice of 2; zest at the END, the oils are volatile

Onion in the oil, 8 minutes on low, no colour. Garlic for 60 seconds.

Peas and spinach in for the last 4 minutes.

Roll into 16 fat fingers and rest them in the fridge 15 minutes if you have it.
Bulgur into a bowl, boiling water to 2cm above it, a plate on top, 12 minutes. Fork it through. Done.

Sauce: peppers in the oil for 6 minutes, cumin and chilli for 60 seconds, passata in, then simmer 12 minutes uncovered until it darkens and thickens. Dukkah over the Skyr.

recipes.name: Crispy duck with puy lentils and braised red cabbage

ingredients.note: about 2.2kg raw on the bone, yields roughly 800g of meat. Thaw 24–36 hours in the fridge
1g on the skin, 1g across the lentils. The skin salt is what dries it out and crisps it

jon.note: 200g of cooked duck meat, 145g cooked lentils, 106g red cabbage, 109g tenderstem

daughter.note: her share is the corpus median, 75% of Jon's - it was a straight copy of Cheryl's

leftover.note: Better cold than warm — shred the meat through the lentils with extra vinegar and eat it as a salad. Reheating makes duck tough.

warnings: Thaw it properly: 24 to 36 hours in the fridge for a whole bird. Not on the worktop, not in water. Start two days before you want to eat it.
Pour the fat off as it renders — 250–350g comes out of a duck this size. Keep it for another day; it's why this plate has lentils, not potatoes.
The skin isn't in the numbers. Even 20g of crisp skin is about +90 kcal.
method: The day before, if you can. Duck out of its wrapping, patted bone dry, skin scored in a diamond through the fat but not into the meat. Rub 1g of the weighed salt over the skin and leave it uncovered on a rack in the fridge overnight. Dry skin is crisp skin; this step does more than anything in the oven.
Oven to 150\u00b0C. Duck breast-up on a rack over a deep tray, 2 hours. Prick the fat pads along the sides every 40 minutes and pour the fat off the tray whenever it collects.

Lentils: onion, garlic and thyme softened in a spoon of the duck fat, lentils in, then the half-strength stock and the bay. Simmer 25 minutes until they hold their shape, then the other 1g of salt. Not soft - puy lentils that collapse are the wrong texture against duck.

Red cabbage: shredded fine, into a pan with the grated apple and the vinegar, lid on, 30 minutes on low, stirred now and then. The vinegar keeps the colour; without it the cabbage goes the colour of a bruise.
Oven to 220\u00b0C for the last 20-25 minutes to blister the skin. Watch it - it goes from brown to black faster than you expect at that temperature.
Rest 20 minutes before carving, loosely covered. Duck tightens if you cut it hot.
Tenderstem in at the very end, 4 minutes in boiling water. Lentils on the plate, duck on top, cabbage beside, and a spoon of the lentil liquor over.

tips.text: Keep the rendered fat. It is the best thing in the house for roast potatoes and it keeps months in the fridge - just not on this plate.
Puy rather than green lentils: they hold their shape against a rich meat where green ones turn to mush.
A whole duck is 2 to 2.2kg raw and yields only about 800g of meat. That is three plates and two lunches and nothing over - do not plan a third meal off it.

leftoverMethod: A leftover lunch is a weighed portion of the same dish, so its macros scale with its weight off that person's own dinner plate - not off the other person's, because the two plates are differently composed. Jon's portions target the middle of the brief's stated 400-550 lunch band. CHERYL HAS NO STATED LUNCH BAND ANYWHERE; hers target 385 kcal, the middle of the 350-420 her own verified week already runs at. That is observed, not ruled on, and needs the coach. The method reproduces the one Cheryl leftover ever hand-costed (Thursday's chilli tub) at 386/37.9 against 387/37.8. RE-DERIVED 19 September 2026 against the new composition table: every portion below is the weight that lands on its target off that person's own re-costed plate, so weight and macros now agree by construction. Jon's target is the 480 kcal lunch slot target; Cheryl's is still the observed 385 and still needs the coach.
portionRule: One recipe, one set of ingredients, one ratio. Jon's plate is the recipe's portion; Cheryl has three-quarters of it (4:3); the daughter's share is whatever her plate weight has always been, of the same food. Nothing is made twice and nobody gets a different version. Set 18 September 2026 after Cheryl had spent a week making two smoothies.
lunchRule: Warming up is fine - reheating a portion, filling a flask, a soup out of the freezer, a few minutes in a pan. PREPARING AND COOKING RAW INGREDIENTS IS NOT: no fish, no raw meat, nothing with a prep stage and a cook stage. That happens the night before or with the weekend batch. Set 19 September 2026, clarified the same day: the line is raw ingredients, not heat.
crispRule: Chef's rule, 19 September: every dish carries one crisp element - 8-15g of toasted seed, nut or breadcrumb. Twenty-one of thirty-three had none, and the dishes this family already likes are, without exception, the ones that do. Costs 45-70 kcal a plate. 19 September re-cost: the jacket potatoes and the barley orzotto were the last two dishes with nothing crisp in them and both now carry a weighed garnish. Every live recipe in the file satisfies the rule.

slotTargets.note: Any combination of these lands within about 50 kcal of 1,900. Set 19 September after the spread between the leanest and heaviest combination turned out to be 641 kcal.

coachRulings.source: Coach rulings, 19 September 2026, in response to handover 4. Brief goes to v5.
coachRulings.efficiencyTest: Ranks protein sources; it never rejects an ingredient. Applies to MEAT, FISH AND DAIRY ONLY. Fat doing work - a cooking medium, a dressing, what carries the spice - is never assessed by it.
coachRulings.cookingWater: Unsalted by default. Where a recipe genuinely needs it, count 20% absorption for pasta and grains and 10% for potatoes and vegetables, marked medium confidence. Dry-brining and salt rubbed on skins that get eaten count 100%. Only crumbed-cod-crushed-potato still salts its water, and it is counted in full.
coachRulings.roundUp: When an absorption estimate is uncertain, round UP. Calories and protein are targets and an error can go either way. Salt is a ceiling, and an error that rounds down is the only kind that can hurt.
coachRulings.crispRule: Ratified. One condition: BREADCRUMBS ARE A STARCH and count against the starch allowance. Seeds and nuts at 8-15g sit outside it. Measured across the corpus on 19 September: a single-starch dinner runs 27-43g of starch-carb on Jon's plate, and the four pangrattato dishes sit at 19-40g, inside it. Only crumbed-cod at 45g was over, and its potatoes came down to bring it to 40g.
coachRulings.chickenNaming: 'Cooked chicken' is not an ingredient. Every line says HOME-ROASTED or PRE-PACKED. Pre-packed is ~1.0g of salt per 100g against 0.16g home-roasted - tenfold, and invisible on the plate.
coachRulings.ceilingsVsTargets: A missing meal suspends a target. It can never suspend a ceiling. Calories and protein are targets and cannot be scored on a day with an uncounted meal. Salt is a ceiling; an untracked meal can only push it up. Same for any future ceiling.
coachRulings.daughter: NO CALORIE OR PROTEIN NUMBERS ARE SHOWN FOR HER, anywhere. Portioned by composition, the same way Cheryl is - she eats the same food in her own share. A teenage girl should not be handed a daily calorie number; that is a wellbeing judgement, not a planning one. If Jon wants her nutrition assessed, that is a GP or a registered dietitian, not this planner and not the coach.
coachRulings.fibre: Reported, never gating. It can never reject a plan or trigger a substitution. Flag only when it is under 25g for three consecutive days, which is a pattern rather than a day. Where fibre competes with calories and protein inside 1,900, fibre loses.
coachRulings.gammon: Three mandatory conditions: simmer in fresh water and DISCARD it - a step, not a tip; once a month maximum; and the leftovers are frozen, not eaten the next day. Gammon is the single exception to 'every dinner leaves a next-day lunch'. The deciding line was the daughter taking 4.04g of salt twice in a week against the same 6g ceiling an adult has.
coachRulings.weeklyTarget: THE TARGET IS WEEKLY: 13,800 kcal. Six counted days at 1,900 +-50 and Saturday at about 2,400, uncounted. A cheat week is every week; there is no other kind. The +611 was never an overage - it is the cheat meal, and it was always budgeted. Do not claw it back on weekdays: a cheat meal with a debt attached is not a cheat meal.
coachRulings.proteinFloor: 170g is a FLOOR, not a target. 167.7g is a fail. Protein is protected ahead of calories in every trade-off: a day light on calories that hits protein is fine, and the reverse is not.
coachRulings.breakfastBase: All seven breakfasts carry the standard dairy base - 200g plain Skyr plus a scoop of whey. A genuinely dairy-free breakfast needs a named iodine source and must be flagged. Almond milk is not one, and at 32 kcal per gram of protein it belongs nowhere near a protein target.

plates_daughter_note: Her column carries PLATE WEIGHTS ONLY - no calories and no protein, anywhere, by coach ruling 3.4 of 19 September. She eats the same food in her own share, portioned by composition exactly as Cheryl is. A teenage girl should not be handed a daily calorie number; that is a wellbeing judgement, not a planning one, and nobody in this system is her dietitian. If her nutrition is to be assessed properly that is a GP or a registered dietitian.
portionConvention: basePortions is how many PLATES the ingredient list makes, and the ingredient list always covers everyone who eats it. Jon is one plate and Cheryl is three-quarters of one, so a two-person lunch is basePortions 2 and its ingredients are 1.75 x Jon's portion. Four lunches were written the other way - basePortions 1 with Jon's portion only - and the shopping list, which scales by portions/basePortions, was buying 2 x Jon for a 1.75 x Jon need. Corrected 20 September 2026.

drainedYields.note: Grams left in the sieve from ONE pack, for ingredients every recipe specifies drained. The shopping list must divide by these, not by the pack's gross weight - a 400g tin of beans is 400g of tin-and-liquid and about 235g of beans. Jon hit this on 21 September: the prawn salad asked for 260g of drained butter beans and the list bought one 400g tin, which cannot contain it.
